front.headline: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
front.dek: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.

brief: Standard Kernel optimized Intel Gaudi2 software, delivering 60% higher Qwen3.5-27B decode throughput than Nvidia H100 at $0.60/hour.

stories.headline: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
stories.dek: GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code. Lab tests found evidence of binding across five targets.
detail: Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs.

An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take.

In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets. Redesigned antibodies also retained binding. Specialized models helped supply sequences and select candidates for testing.
The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules.

stories.headline: Standard Kernel optimizes Intel Gaudi2 to surpass Nvidia H100 in Qwen3.5 decode
stories.dek: Software optimizations brought a 3.21-times cached-prefill boost to Intel's Gaudi2, yielding higher token throughput than an Nvidia H100.
detail: Software firm Standard Kernel has published optimizations for Intel’s four-year-old Gaudi2 accelerators, achieving a 3.21-times increase in cached-prefill throughput and a 2.84-times increase in decode throughput. In benchmarks running the Qwen 3.5-27B model, a single optimized Gaudi2 delivered 60 per cent higher decode throughput and 8 per cent higher prefill throughput than a single Nvidia H100 80 GB PCIe card.

The performance gain was accomplished through targeted systems software changes without hardware modifications. Standard Kernel reduced prefill padding using finer 128-token buckets, accelerated prefill attention by separating cached prefixes from causal suffixes, simplified matrix inversions with custom TPC kernels, and fused decode operations such as convolution, activation, and normalization into single kernels.

While Gaudi2 features 96 GB of VRAM operating at 2.45 TB/s compared to the H100’s 3.35 TB/s bandwidth, its lower rental pricing significantly alters cost efficiency. Available to rent at $0.60 per hour versus $3.50 per hour for the H100, the optimized Gaudi2 provides 9.4 times more tokens per dollar on the tested workload. However, Intel has since abandoned its Gaudi roadmap, leaving its future AI hardware direction focused primarily on the upcoming Crescent Island family.
stories.why: Shows how targeted software kernel fusions and bucket optimizations can drastically reduce cloud GPU rental costs when serving large open-weight models.

stories.headline: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
stories.dek: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.
detail: Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going.

According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.

As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.
Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’

stories.headline: Hugging Face launches llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
stories.dek: A new public dashboard allows developers to track local LLM inference performance across AMD hardware configurations and llama.cpp builds.
detail: Hugging Face has released the llama.cpp x AMD Benchmark dashboard, providing a public platform to inspect prompt processing and text generation speeds on AMD Ryzen and Radeon hardware. The tool tracks performance changes across software builds, model architectures, and quantization schemes over time.

The benchmark suite currently covers hardware targets such as the Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) and Radeon AI Pro R9700S (gfx1201). Tests are run using the standard llama-bench tool with Flash Attention enabled and disabled across various GGUF formats, including Q4_K_M, Q8_0, BF16, and F16.

Evaluated workloads focus on two key metrics starting at context depth zero: PP512, which measures processing throughput for 512 input tokens without generation, and TG128, which measures generation throughput for 128 tokens. Benchmark workflows run on a weekly schedule using prebuilt binaries from llama-install.sh, reading directly from a public Hugging Face Storage Bucket.
stories.why: Provides reproducible benchmarks to track how software updates and GGUF quantizations alter model throughput on accessible hardware.

stories.headline: TSMC certifies 1.4nm A14 node design flows with Cadence and Synopsys
stories.dek: Chip designers can now build for TSMC's 1.4nm-class A14 process ahead of planned 2028 high-volume production.
detail: TSMC has announced that certified EDA design flows from Cadence and Synopsys are now available for its A14 manufacturing node. The 1.4nm-class node serves as the full-node successor to TSMC’s 2nm N2 process, with risk and pilot production scheduled for 2027 and high-volume production expected in 2028.

The A14 node introduces second-generation gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and an updated standard-cell architecture named NanoFlex Pro. A key feature of NanoFlex Pro is the inclusion of Boost Cells, which combine tall, high-performance logic cells for critical timing paths with short, energy-efficient cells for non-critical areas. TSMC projects a 25 to 30 per cent power reduction at equivalent performance levels compared to previous nodes.

TSMC has opted not to integrate High-NA EUV lithography for the initial A14 deployment, choosing instead to maintain existing toolsets to keep production costs accessible. Front-side power delivery will be used initially, with a backside power delivery variant named Super Power Rail scheduled to follow in 2029.
stories.why: Highlights incoming semiconductor efficiency gains that will impact future cloud compute availability and power constraints for hardware clusters.

stories.headline: Hugging Face publishes framework for training and evaluating multi-agent systems
stories.dek: A new blog series details decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning techniques and practical methods for evaluating communication overhead.
detail: Hugging Face has published the first entry in a series focused on building, training, and evaluating multi-agent systems using small language models. The series addresses technical challenges in multi-agent execution, where adding agents increases context complexity, token usage, and overall budget demands without guaranteeing superior performance over a single model.

The guide examines multi-agent systems through the framework of decentralized partially observable Markov decision processes (Dec-POMDPs). To handle credit assignment and dynamic peer behavior during training, it highlights centralized training with decentralized execution, where models learn from shared team rewards while executing independently based on partial observations.

As a reproducible baseline, the post details an information-sharing task featuring four agents that share a language model to aggregate assigned numbers into a sorted list. The author emphasizes measuring whether agent communication provides genuine performance gains or merely consumes compute that could otherwise be allocated to scaling single-agent token budgets.
stories.why: Offers practical insights into Dec-POMDP mechanics and budget trade-offs when orchestrating smaller language models in multi-agent workflows.

india.headline: Chariot AI launches 11B MoE model and Indic TTS under IndiaAI Mission
india.dek: Noida-based startup Chariot AI unveiled its Chariot-1 suite, featuring an 11 billion parameter MoE LLM and novel Indic language optimizations.
detail: Noida-headquartered startup Chariot AI has launched its Chariot-1 model suite at a MeitY event under the IndiaAI Mission. The suite includes an 11 billion parameter mixture-of-experts language model with 4 billion active parameters per token, alongside a context-aware text-to-speech model supporting 10 Indian languages.

The LLM is available in three sizes: 10.7 billion, 1.7 billion, and 745 million parameters. It was trained from scratch in India using three technical innovations: IndicShift, Nested Training, and Mixture of Vocabularies. IndicShift introduces a shared 350-letter alphabet across 12 Indian scripts, reducing token usage on Indian text by up to 2.5 times and improving model performance by 5 to 8 per cent on equivalent compute.

Nested Training allows all three model sizes to train simultaneously in a single run, reducing overall training time by 62 per cent. Additionally, Mixture of Vocabularies divides the vocabulary into 11 groups to score only relevant subsets during output, improving GPU training speed by 38 per cent. The TTS model demonstrated a Hindi character error rate of 7.60 per cent and an average character error rate of 6.47 per cent across nine other Indian languages on evaluation benchmarks.
india.why: Demonstrates how shared script tokenization and nested training architectures can significantly lower training compute costs for multilingual Indic foundation models.

india.headline: An Indic Voice Agent with CUGA
detail: Most useful knowledge is written and digitized in English. Most of the people who need it speak, and think, in their own regional languages like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Marathi and many others. Many would rather talk than type.
We built a small voice agent to close that gap, using CUGA as the agent harness. This post explains the use case and what we learned. You can try it yourself in CUGA Apps.
A farmer asks a question aloud, in their own language: how do I tell good seed from bad? The agent:
Answers in two to four spoken sentences, in the language the question was asked in, using only what the handbook says.

india.headline: Thomas Dohmke’s Entire Partners With Sarvam to Bring AI Coding Agents to India
india.dek: Under the partnership, Sarvam’s models will be available in preview on Trails, Entire’s alternative to the traditional pull request.
detail: Entire has partnered with Sarvam to introduce AI coding agents for Indian developers, ensuring data residency in India.
The integration of Sarvam's models on Entire's Trails platform allows for private code hosting and agent inference within India.
This collaboration aims to support organisations in regulated industries by keeping code and data within the country.
Thomas Dohmke believes India can lead in agent-human collaboration, producing significant amounts of code while maintaining AI sovereignty.
